research_mode: official MHCLG and ONS primary sources only; latest England fire-and-rescue statistics, CSEW quality/methodology and crime-statistics user-guide gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Outdoor-primary-fire annual change
verified_claims: 6,924 outdoor primary fires were attended in the year ending March 2026, 48% more than the previous year
limitations: the annual comparison is strongly affected by seasonal and weather conditions

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Secondary-fire annual count
verified_claims: 102,549 secondary fires were attended in the year ending March 2026
limitations: secondary-fire volume must not be treated as a building-fire count

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Purpose-built high-rise fire count
verified_claims: 695 fires were attended in purpose-built high-rise flats or maisonettes of 10 or more storeys in the year ending March 2026
limitations: an incident count without the number of buildings or exposure denominator is not a risk rate

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Weather effect on fire counts
verified_claims: hot and dry summers in 2018, 2022 and 2025 contributed to high numbers of outdoor primary and secondary fires
limitations: weather-sensitive annual counts require contextual adjustment before trend interpretation

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Building-fire annual count
verified_claims: 39,859 building fires were attended in the year ending March 2026 and building fires accounted for 60% of primary fires
limitations: the aggregate count does not establish whether a named building had an incident

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire false-alarm definition
verified_claims: a fire false alarm is an attendance where the service expected a fire but found that no fire incident existed
limitations: a false-alarm attendance is not evidence of an actual fire

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: False alarm due to apparatus definition
verified_claims: false alarms due to apparatus occur when a fire alarm or firefighting equipment operates in error, including accidental initiation
limitations: the category does not prove equipment failure at a particular property without incident-level evidence

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Good-intent false-alarm definition
verified_claims: good-intent false alarms are calls made in good faith believing the service would be attending a fire
limitations: the category records caller belief rather than a confirmed hazard

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Malicious false-alarm definition
verified_claims: malicious fire false alarms are made with the intention of causing attendance at a non-existent incident
limitations: the aggregate category does not identify an offender or location

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire false-alarm annual total
verified_claims: 255,047 fire false alarms were attended in the year ending March 2026
limitations: the national total is not a measure of actual fire prevalence

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Non-fire incident scope
verified_claims: non-fire incidents include flooding, road traffic collisions, animal assistance, effecting entry or exit and assistance to other agencies
limitations: the service category is heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into a single parcel-risk indicator

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Non-fire incident annual total
verified_claims: 215,583 non-fire incidents were attended in the year ending March 2026, the largest financial-year figure since consistent data became available
limitations: the count represents fire-service attendance and not all emergency demand

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Non-fire presentation-grouping revision
verified_claims: recent releases regrouped non-fire incident types using existing FaRDaP categories and applied the presentation change retrospectively
limitations: the regrouping did not change underlying definitions, recording practices or coverage and must not be treated as a new incident series

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Collaboration-incident category composition
verified_claims: collaboration incidents combine assisting other agencies, effecting entry or exit, and suicide or suicide-attempt categories
limitations: the combined category does not permit inference about any one component at parcel level

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fire-fatality definition and revision gate
verified_claims: fire-related fatalities are deaths that would not otherwise have occurred without a fire, and FaRDaP figures can be revised after coroners' reports
limitations: published fatality figures may differ from local records and are not immutable
